title: Product-total Hom comparison from its projection equations
statement: Let B and A be preadditive categories, U : B → A an additive functor preserving products indexed by the integers, and HB, HA bifunctors contravariant in the first variable. Let FB, FA be functors from pairs of complexes to complexes, equipped with projections exhibiting each degree as the product of HB(K^p,I^(p+n)), respectively HA(K^p,I^(p+n)). Assume their differential projections are d_I f minus (-1)^n f d_K, and their map projections are precomposition followed by postcomposition. Given a natural isomorphism U HB(M,N) ≅ HA(UM,UN), there is a natural chain isomorphism U FB(K,I) ≅ FA(UK,UI). Its composite with every product projection is U applied to the source projection followed by precisely the given bifunctor comparison.

source.place: Sections 0A8X and 08J7, Lemma 0A95; componentwise and localization assembly from steps 4–5 of lem-sf-ringed-forget-two-injective-hom.

proof.text: Apply preservation of integer-indexed products to the source product cone supplied as a hypothesis. Postcompose its factors with the given bifunctor comparison. Both this cone and the given target product cone are limits of the same diagram, so cone-point uniqueness gives a term isomorphism satisfying the exact projection equation.

Test the differential identity on each target product projection. Use the assumed differential-projection equations. Additivity preserves subtraction and the integer-unit sign. Naturality of the given bifunctor comparison identifies postcomposition and precomposition separately; product-cone uniqueness then gives equality of differentials.

Test naturality on every degree and target projection. Use the assumed map-projection formulas. The remaining equation is naturality of the bifunctor comparison. Assemble the degree isomorphisms into chain isomorphisms and then a natural isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Formal categorical assembly of the product-total Hom and K-injective models in Sections 0A8X and 08J7.

theorem ringedHomComplexComparison :
    ∃ chain : FB ⋙ U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ≅
      ((U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).op.prod (U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ))) ⋙ FA,
      ∀ (K I : CochainComplex B ℤ) (n p q : ℤ) (hpq : p + n = q),
        (chain.hom.app (op K, I)).f n ≫
            πA ((U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K)
              ((U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj I) n p q hpq =
          U.map (πB K I n p q hpq) ≫ h.hom.app (op (K.X p), I.X q)
